title: Purity for the punctured spectrum of a regular local ring
statement: Let A be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of Krull dimension at least two [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let U be the open complement of its closed point in Spec A [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Every finite etale morphism Y -> U [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism] extends to a finite etale morphism F -> Spec A together with an isomorphism Y to its restriction to U over U.

source.place: Tag 0BMA, pione-lemma-purity-regular, assertion (1); Tags 0BM9 and 0BLM for the normal-algebra and lifting criteria

proof.text: Use the maximal ideal spanFinrank as the finite natural dimension and strongly induct on it. In dimension two obtain the finite flat model with depth-two boundary. Transfer etaleness from q to the restricted model via its over-U isomorphism and apply flat quasi-finite depth-two purity.

For dimension d at least three choose a minimal finite generating list rs of the maximal ideal. Its length is d by regularity. The generators theorem makes it regular and its quotient by the first generator f regular of dimension d-1. The regular sequence witnesses depth at least d, hence at least three. The quotient spectrum embeds into Spec A and sends its closed point to the closed point, so the inverse image of U is exactly its punctured spectrum.

Base change q to this quotient punctured spectrum; finiteness and etaleness persist. Apply strong induction at dimension d-1 to the actual pullback and feed that extension to depth-three lifting. This finishes the inductive step, including empty covers.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finite_etale_extension_of_regular_local_punctured_spectrum
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsRegularLocalRing A]
    (hdim : (2 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim A)
    (U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens)
    (hU : ∀ x : Spec (.of A), x ∈ U ↔ x ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint A)
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (q : Y ⟶ U.toScheme) [IsFinite q] [Etale q] :
    ∃ (F : Scheme.{u}) (r : F ⟶ Spec (.of A)), IsFinite r ∧ Etale r ∧
      ∃ e : Y ≅ (r ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme, e.hom ≫ r ∣_ U = q
